decisions.executionNote: Bend left arm into elbow-up approach above the table; mallet is nearer the center and more horizontal than the reference, so grasp will be visually aligned next.
Translate left hand toward the mallet butt while rotating toward a downward pinch aligned with its diagonal handle. Keep right arm parked.
Complete downward gripper alignment and approach above the near end of the mallet, leaving clearance to inspect the pinch location.
Fine-align shaft between fingers from wrist view and lower 22 mm to the grasp height; keep the mallet supported until closure.
Wrist view shows shaft right of the pinch center; correct laterally at constant height before closing.
Center the handle at the pinch point, then close left gripper fully without translating. Retention still needs a lift check.
Lift the closed grasp 70 mm to verify mallet retention, and begin swinging the shaft toward the keys while staying in the left workspace.
Mallet is visibly retained. Swing toward a forward-pointing striking pose while raising clear of all keys and approaching the leftmost red key.
Align retained mallet above the leftmost red key, correcting leftward and toward the near edge while lowering only partway to inspect the tip.
Lower vertically onto the first red key with a controlled stroke, keeping the grasp closed and watching for contact or mallet displacement.
Finish the first-key downstroke with a small centering correction, then lift 56 mm before any movement to the next key.
Move one key right while lifted, strike the second (orange) key vertically, and lift 60 mm before continuing.
Continue left-to-right to the third yellow key: translate while raised, perform a vertical strike, and lift 60 mm.
Corrected rejected tensor; no motion occurred. Move to fourth green key, strike vertically, and lift 60 mm before arranging a handover.
Raise clear after the fourth-key stroke and rotate the held shaft toward vertical for a central handover; keep the left wrist on its own side.
Continue presenting the shaft upright on the left side; bring the open right arm inward in an elbow-up configuration for a handover.
Finish upright presentation with the left grip closed. Approach from the right with opposing open fingers, stopping short for visual handover alignment.
Replanned from interrupted poses with much smaller left rotation increments. Bring right fingers opposite the upright shaft while preserving both elbow-up configurations.
Right wrist shows the upright shaft centered between opposing fingers. Close the right grip while the left continues supporting it; verify visually before releasing left.
Release the left fingers only after the right has enclosed the shaft, then separate gently to verify the mallet follows the closed right grip.
Mallet follows the right grip after release. Withdraw the left arm and begin rotating the right-held mallet toward the remaining keys, staying elevated.
Continue rotating the right mallet toward a downward striking grip over the cyan key; withdraw left toward its home side without crossing.
Finish right-arm downward grip orientation above the fifth cyan key; keep the mallet elevated for alignment and finish parking the left arm.
The tip is aligned over the cyan key after handover. Lower 30 mm vertically to inspect contact height without moving laterally.
Continue the fifth-key vertical downstroke cautiously, inspecting the mallet tip at the key surface before lifting.
Finish the cyan-key contact with a small additional downstroke, then lift the retained mallet 60 mm before advancing.
Advance one key right to blue while raised, strike vertically at the established contact height, then lift 60 mm.
Move to the seventh purple key while lifted, slightly center the tip away from the near edge, strike, and lift 60 mm.
Advance to the rightmost magenta key, strike vertically, then lift 72 mm to complete the final release with the mallet retained.
